newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds slide, spreads modestly wider.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds slide, spreads modestly wider.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities declined modestly in line with Treasuries on Wednesday, traders said.
Mortgages traded heavily among both retail clients and dealers, but spreads moved little, traders said.
"Pass-throughs traded a little heavy today," one trader said. "Spreads are just a touch wider."
At 1530 EST/2030 GMT, mortgages were unchanged to off 4/32 overall, while comparable Treasuries were down 2/32 to 4/32.
The February consumer prices report, which was slightly higher than expected, set the bearish tone, analysts said.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was off 3/32 at 98-30/32, yielding 103 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were off 3/32 as well, at 99-00/32 and 99-06/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was down 4/32 at 96-16/32 to yield 6.74 percent.
Consumer prices rose 0.3 percent in February after a 0.1 percent rise in January, an increase one analyst described as "marginally disappointing."
